title: Course Schedule II
statement_short: Given the total number of courses numCourses and a list of prerequisite pairs, return the ordering of courses you should take to finish all courses. Return an empty array if it is impossible to finish all courses.
constraints: 1 <= numCourses <= 2000, 0 <= prerequisites.length <= 5000, prerequisites[i].length == 2, all pairs are unique
hint: Dependencies up to 2000 nodes require constructing a valid linear order of directed graph nodes.
keywords: empty array if it is impossible
why_not: Right: Topological Sort uses Kahn's algorithm (in-degree queue) to output a valid linear ordering of graph nodes in O(V + E) time. Not Graph DFS: Standard DFS traverses graph paths but requires post-order stack reversal to produce topological node ordering. Not Tree BFS: Level-order tree traversal assumes hierarchical parent-child nodes rather than arbitrary directed graph edges. Not Backtracking: Permutating all node sequences causes TLE compared to linear topological sorting.
complexity: O(V + E) time, O(V + E) space
